- Thm A (g-form): (1-q)P = B(q)(1-q^{rb})/(1-q^r) = G(q)(1-q^{rb}) with G = sum g_i q^i, so P_i - P_{i-1} = g_i - g_{i-rb}; a palindromic nonnegative sequence is unimodal iff nondecreasing on [0,floor(N/2)] (z3-verified for lengths 1..9, general argument trivial). OK. Brute force: identity and equivalence held on all 134,726 exhaustive tuples (every b in [1,T6+5]).
- Thm C (b <= T6 = 1+floor((D+1-2mu)/r) when r divides no a_i): my proof: P_i = Gamma_{i mod r} for max(0,D+1-r) <= i <= rb-1 (plateau; numerically verified, 3000 random cases); the plateau is symmetric about N/2; unimodality forces P nonincreasing on the L = rb - ceil(N/2) = floor((r(b+1)-D)/2) indices [ceil(N/2), rb-1], whose residues are r-L..r-1; if L >= r+1 Gamma would be constant, impossible since A(zeta_r) != 0 when r divides no a_i (verified numerically both directions); if L <= r the condition is tau_j <= 0 for j in [r-L+1,r-1], i.e. mu <= r-L, which is equivalent to b <= T6 (z3: ThmC_arith); plateau validity rb >= D+2-r (z3: ThmC_plateau, ThmC_L) and the complementary range rb <= D+1-r gives b <= T6 directly (z3: ThmC_trivial). OK. Brute force: 0 violations on 134,726 tuples. Also mu(tau-definition) == mu(Gamma-definition) on all tuples (0 mismatches).
Lemma 1 (symmetry g_i = tau_{i mod r} + g_{D+1-r-i}): each step checked (palindromicity of A, B_{D+1-j} = -B_j, index substitution, boundary conventions). OK. 0 failures on all exhaustive tuples, i in [0,D+2r).
Lemma 2 (FIRE kills T6-1, T6): step 1 (FIRE => D+1 >= r since otherwise tau_s = -1) OK; step 2 floor identity z3-valid (L2_step2); step 3 g_{i0} = tau_s + 1 <= -1 OK (also numerically); step 4 inequalities i0 >= 0, i0 < rb, 2 i0 <= N z3-valid (L2_step4, L2_Qge1); step 5 OK via Thm A. Brute force: 1,206 firing general tuples + 156 firing non-base 3-middle tuples + 8,914 firing base tuples, 0 failures.
Lemma 3 (peeling): q-identity verified algebraically (four monomials) and numerically (0 failures/3000); decomposition, degrees/center M = D+rb OK; step 4 standard; steps 5-6 z3-valid for lengths 1..9, general argument immediate. Implication tested on 2,216 random cases, 0 failures. Corollary 3' induction OK (a' entries stay >= 1 since rho_i >= 1; deleting [1]_q factors harmless).
Lemma 4 (invariance): D(a) = D(rho)+rF OK; [a]_q = [rho]_q + q^rho [r]_q [f]_{q^r} and (1-q)[r]_q = 1-q^r kills the extra terms mod q^r-1, so tau, mu, s, FIRE agree OK; floor step z3-valid (L4_step3). 0 failures numerically on all tuples.
Lemma 5 (base family computation): count C(30,4)*38 = 1,041,390 matches; inputs regenerated by my own generator and diffed identical. Fully RERUN with my own independent C program u256.c (two-limb unsigned __int128 256-bit two's complement, computes P_i = S_i - S_{i-rb} via prefix sums rather than the explorer's g array, checks nondecreasing on first half); overflow bound |values| <= prod a_i <= 29^40 < 2^195 OK. Result: 1,041,390 instances, 0 overflow, 0 with U != [1,B*], min B* = 1, 8,914 firing instances, 0 line-level mismatches with the explorer's base_out_*.txt. Cross-validation of u256 by Python big-int raw-definition unimodality (no palindromic shortcut, no g-form): 244 random tuples incl. 18 with prod >= 2^127 (xval.py), 120 random large base tuples with k >= 28 (xval2.py), ALL 7,980 base tuples with r <= 10 (py_small_base.py): 0 mismatches. PARI/GP (GMP) independent check: all 8,914 firing base tuples + 4,000 random base tuples = 12,914 cases, 0 mismatches (gp_big.log final line 'gp cases 12914 bad 0'; an earlier gp run with the default 8MB stack overflowed and was rerun with -s 2000000000). 2% Python subsample of rule values (T6, F, B*) from the input lines: 0 mismatches.
Proof of THEOREM: steps 1-4 assemble correctly (residue vector with 1's deleted is a base tuple with same r, nm; lower bound via Cor 3' + Lemma 5 + Lemma 4; upper bound via Thm C or Lemma 2; B*(rho) >= 1 confirmed so [1,F] union (F+[1,B*(rho)]) is an interval). Direct tests of the theorem on non-base tuples (F>0, residue-1 entries, a_i up to ~5r): 389 random instances (9 firing) + 156 firing-only instances, 0 failures; exhaustive in-domain tuples: 68,646 (k<=4, a<=16, r<=10; k<=3, a<=29, r<=30), 0 failures. v.reasons: Every step of the proof holds. The two 'cited' results (Thm A, Thm C) are not in the source paper, but both are provable with short arguments which I supplied and verified (Thm C via the plateau P_i = Gamma_{i mod r} on [D+1-r, rb-1], non-constancy of Gamma when r divides no a_i, and a z3-checked inequality chain). The reduction of the general claim (arbitrary a_i sizes, arbitrary number of residue-1 entries) to the base family via Corollary 3' (lower bound) and Thm C/Lemma 2 (upper bound) is logically complete, and the claimed statement matches the proved theorem. Scope correctly stated: nothing is claimed for r>=31 or nm>=38.

v.reasons: The claimed numbers do not reproduce. The claim gives no definition of its parameter family or of 'Conjecture S2'; the unique natural family with exactly 100,488 sets (r in [4,8], k<=6, 1<=a_i<=2r+1, r∤a_i, multisets) yields B_main-B_off = 1 in 100,408 and 3 in 80 by two independent implementations (numpy and C) plus a sympy spot-check, not the claimed 100,402 / 86. The value 86 arises only on families of different size (a<=2r+2: 142,943 sets; box a<=17: 228,679 sets), so the claimed pair (100,488 total; 100,402/86 split) is internally inconsistent with any family I could identify. The claim's B_off ('max element of U with parity F') is also undefined for sets with F=0 and U={1}, which occur in every candidate family. The qualitative structure (prefix {1..F+1}⊆U, B_main odd relative to F, differences only 1 and 3) does hold on all ~700k sets I tested in and out of range, but the specific numerical claim is not reproduced, so by the stated standard the verdict is REJECT.
